product_summary: Website mathaexports.com (self-described 'Matha Exports International', President Bineesh Joseph) presents a very broad herbal/botanical catalogue, not a food/FMCG range: (1) henna and hair-dye powders — Natural Henna, Indigo Powder, Black/Brown/Burgundy/Mahogany Henna, henna-based permanent hair dyes, henna tattoo powder (HS 1404.90 vegetable products n.e.s. / 3203.00 dyeing matter of vegetable origin); (2) ~70 herbal powders — Amla, Ashwagandha, Brahmi, Bhringraj, Triphala, Moringa leaf/seed, Neem, Shikakai, Soapnut, Senna leaves & pods, Psyllium husk & seeds, Stevia, Tulsi, Ginger, Turmeric, Cinnamon, Curry leaves, Tamarind, Tomato, Beetroot, Wheat grass, Spirulina (HS 1211.90, 1302.19 saps/extracts & pectin/mucilage, 1213.00, 0910.99, 0906.11, 0908.31, 0909.21, 0910.20, 1212.21, 0712.90, 0902.10/0902.40, 2101.11); (3) certified-organic oils — coconut, neem, amla, bhringraj, brahmi, shikakai hair oils (HS 3305.90, 1513.19, 3301.29); (4) herbal face masks / ubtan / sandal, orange, neem, rose masks (HS 3304.99); (5) herbal shampoo, conditioner, hair tonic, hair pack (HS 3305.90); (6) brown rice flour (HS 1102.90), fuller's earth / dead sea mud clay (HS 2508.40), guar gum powder (HS 1302.32), cassia alata/obovata, ratanjot, red kamala, katha, jamun, gokshura, gymnema, mulethi, punarnava-type botanicals.
comment: Declared 1302.19 ('saps and extracts of vegetable products') is only PARTIALLY correct: it plausibly covers the extract/powder-type botanicals (ashwagandha, amla, brahmi, gymnema, mucilage/guar-type items), but it is not the correct heading for the company's core line — henna/indigo hair-dye powders, which are HS 1404.90 (vegetable products n.e.s.) or 3203.00 (dyeing matter of vegetable origin), nor for the finished cosmetic lines (hair oils, shampoos, face masks → 3305.90 / 3304.99) and the food-grade items (psyllium husk 1211.90/1213.00, spices 0906/0908/0909/0910, rice flour 1102.90, coffee 2101.11). So: partial match, with the dominant product (henna) sitting outside the declared code. Per project rule 3 this is NOT a rejection ground — the company stays in the base and the code must be corrected to the actual mix (lead codes 1404.90 + 1302.19 + 1211.90 + 3305.90). Industry label 'Продукты питания и FMCG' is a misclassification: the catalogue is dominated by herbal/botanical and cosmetic/personal-care goods (hair dyes, hair oils, face masks), with only a minority of edible items (psyllium, spices, flours, coffee, stevia). Trader signs: the site simultaneously claims 'Cultivator, Manufacturer and Exporter' and 'supplies ... to wholesalers', and the range spans ~100 SKUs across unrelated categories (clay, guar gum, henna dye, face cream, coffee) — consistent with a mixed manufacturer_trader / aggregator model rather than a single-line producer; no factory/plant address or unit capacity is published on the page read. Product lines missing from the declaration: henna and indigo dye powders, henna-based permanent hair dyes, herbal hair oils, shampoos/conditioners/tonics, face masks/ubtan, fuller's earth and dead-sea clay, brown rice flour, coffee powder, guar gum. All product claims are from the company's own website only — no customs line, B/L or GST record was checked in this task, therefore every product line is 'заявлено, не подтверждено'. Note: the site brands itself 'Matha Exports International' without the 'LLP' suffix, so the identity link between the website and the registered LLP 'MATHA EXPORTS INTERNATIONAL LLP' is asserted, not verified here (registry check out of scope). Search tooling was partly unavailable (DuckDuckGo backend refused connections; Bing returned irrelevant results), so no independent third-party catalogue corroboration was obtained.
